The '''2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kentucky]] during the [[college basketball]] season of [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]]. This season was the first of [[John Calipari]]'s tenure as [[head coach]]; he accepted the position on March 31, 2009.

The Wildcats set several records this season. They became the first men's college basketball program to reach 2,000 wins by defeating the [[Drexel Dragons]] on December 21.<ref name="SI.com 2,000 wins">{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/ncaa/men/gameflash/2009/12/21/58979_recap.html?xid=si_topstories|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628214413/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/ncaa/men/gameflash/2009/12/21/58979_recap.html?xid=si_topstories|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 28, 2011|title=No. 3 Kentucky beats Drexel to reach 2,000 wins|date=December 21, 2009|work=SI.com|publisher=Time Warner Company|access-date=22 December 2009|location=Lexington, Kentucky}}</ref> Coach Calipari set a record for the most consecutive wins for a first-year Kentucky basketball coach at 19–0, surpassing [[Adolph Rupp]]'s previous mark of 11–0. Kentucky also extended their existing records for most wins all-time, SEC regular-season championships, SEC tournament championships, NCAA tournament berths, and NCAA tournament wins.

The team was briefly ranked #1 in both the ESPN/Coaches poll and AP poll, and posted the best record in the NCAA (35–3)<ref>{{cite web

===SEC Awards===

==<span class="anchor" id="2010 NBA draft"></span>2010 NBA draft==

On April 7 five players announced their intentions to enter the [[2010 NBA draft]]. Five players declared themselves eligible for the draft: Bledsoe, Cousins, Orton, Patterson, and Wall.<ref name=UKNBA>{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/news/sports_m-baskbl_spec-rel_040710aaa_html|title=Five Wildcats to Put Names in NBA Draft|access-date=2015-11-18|date=2010-04-07|publisher=JMI Sports|work=UKAthletics|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119050807/http://www.ukathletics.com/news/sports_m-baskbl_spec-rel_040710aaa_html|archive-date=2015-11-19|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=UKAPNBA>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2010/news/story?id=5064967|title=Wall among those headed to NBA|access-date=2015-11-18|date=2010-04-08|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> Leading up to the draft Wall, Cousins, and Patterson were projected as lottery picks. Meanwhile, Bledsoe and Orton were projected as possible first-round draft picks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/05/18/consensus.mock/|title=2010 NBA Draft: Consensus Mock Draft|access-date=2010-05-18|date=2010-05-18|publisher=NBA|author=Packham, Drew|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131227175246/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/05/18/consensus.mock/|archive-date=2013-12-27|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the draft Wall was selected No. 1 by Washington. He was followed by Cousins, who went to the [[Sacramento Kings]] at No. 5; Patterson, who was taken by the [[Houston Rockets]] at No. 14; Bledsoe, who was chosen No. 18 by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]; and Orton, who was chosen No. 29 by the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref name=UKDRAFT>{{cite web|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article44037771.html|title=UK makes history with five NBA draft picks in the first round|access-date=2015-06-25|date=2010-06-24|work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]}}</ref> Wall became the first player in Kentucky history taken first in the draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/news/sports_m-baskbl_spec-rel_062410aag_html|title=Five Wildcats Selected in First Round of NBA Draft|access-date=2015-11-18|date=2010-06-24|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKAthletics|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119065518/http://www.ukathletics.com/news/sports_m-baskbl_spec-rel_062410aag_html|archive-date=2015-11-19|url-status=dead}}</ref> The five players taken in the first round tied the record for most players taken from one school in the first round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2010/columns/story?columnist=katz_andy&page=katzoncats-100624|title=Five Wildcats taken in first round|access-date=2015-06-25|date=2010-06-24|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Katz, Andy}}</ref>
